title: It felt like love.
paragraphs:
It felt like love.
But heaven called it betrayal.

And here’s the part that should shake you—
Judas didn’t use violence to identify Jesus.
He used affection.
A kiss became the signal for arrest.
Let that sit on your chest for a moment.

Because not everything that feels close to you is sent by God.
Not everything that looks like love is loyal.
Not everything that sounds like care is clean.
And if we’re honest…

Sometimes the Judas isn’t just around us.
Sometimes it’s within us.

You’ve said, “Lord, I love You”—
but delayed obedience when it cost too much.
You’ve lifted your hands in worship—
but lowered your standards in secret.
You’ve looked pure in public—
but entertained compromise in private.
That’s the kiss.

That moment where your lips say devotion,
but your heart negotiates disobedience.

Jesus said in Luke 6:46, “Why do you call Me ‘Lord, Lord,’ and not do what I say?”
Not to shame you—
but to expose the gap between affection and allegiance.
Here’s the uncomfortable truth:

You can express love for God…
and still resist surrender to God.
Read that again.

Some of us have mastered the language of faith
without embracing the lifestyle of faith.

We know how to sound close to God.
We just don’t stay close to Him when it matters.
And nobody sees it.

Not your pastor.
Not your friends.
Not even your family.
But heaven sees it.

Because God doesn’t measure your love by your words.
He measures it by your obedience.

Jesus said in John 14:15, “If you love Me, keep My commandments.”
Not perform.
Not pretend.
Not post.
Obey.
Let me ask you something that might hit deeper than you expected:

Are you kissing Jesus…
or following Him?
Because those are not always the same.

There’s a kind of Christianity that feels real—
but never transforms you.
A kind of devotion that looks passionate—
but avoids the cross.
A kind of faith that sings loudly—
but surrenders quietly… never.
That’s not love.
That’s proximity without purity.
AHA REVELATION:

Not all closeness is covenant.
Some people are near Jesus… and still betray Him.
SPIRITUAL MIRROR:

You don’t drift from God overnight.
You drift through small compromises you refuse to confront.

Where have you been pretending everything is okay with God…
when deep down, you know it’s not?

Where have you delayed obedience…
hoping emotion would cover what surrender requires?

Because here’s the danger—
the longer you live in hidden compromise,
the more normal it feels.

Until conviction fades.
Until truth feels optional.
Until your “kiss” becomes routine.
And that’s where many stay.

Religious.
Active.
But inwardly distant.
But here’s where grace breaks in.

Jesus knew Judas would betray Him.
He still called him friend in Matthew 26:50.
Friend.

Not because Judas was faithful—
but because Jesus is.
And that’s the Gospel.

Not that we loved perfectly—
but that Christ loved us first.

Romans 5:8 says, “While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
Not after you fixed yourself.
Not after you proved your loyalty.

While you were still inconsistent.
Still struggling.
Still divided.
He chose the cross anyway.
That means this:

Your failure does not disqualify you.
But your refusal to repent will keep you stuck.
There is a way back.

Not through performance.
Not through pretending harder.
Through repentance.
Through surrender.

Through coming to Jesus honestly—
not with a kiss…
but with a broken heart.
Psalm 51:17 says, “A broken and contrite heart, O God, You will not despise.”
Here’s the line that might confront you—but free you:
God is not impressed with your worship if your will is still your own.

But He is ready—right now—
to receive you fully.

You are not called to fake devotion.
You are called to live surrendered.

You are not meant to manage sin quietly.
You are meant to walk in freedom boldly.

And Jesus didn’t just expose false love—
He died to restore real love.
So come back.

Not halfway.
Not later.
Now.

Lay down the hidden thing.
Confess the quiet compromise.
Surrender the area you’ve been protecting.
He’s not waiting to reject you.
He’s waiting to restore you.
If this pierced something in you, don’t ignore it.
Not hype. Transformation.
Stay close.
Follow if you’re ready to grow—God is not done speaking.
And next… we’re exposing the silent habits that slowly replace real intimacy with God.
